The effective line reads max_running_requests=12. So the edit moved the ceiling from 10 to 12, not to 32.
why_the_knob_was_inert.cap_2_harness: the harness's own priority gate admits 10 streams -- the env dict sets 'ARC3_MAX_ACTIVE_STREAMS': 10 under USE_PRIORITY_SCHEDULING and the run logs 'priority gate active: 10 concurrent streams'. Two independent caps sat at ~10-12.
why_the_knob_was_inert.the_arithmetic: tokens available per game = aggregate tok/s x wall clock / number of games. The wall clock (540 min) and the number of private games are both fixed, so concurrency cannot change how much model time each game gets: it can only change WHICH games are served. That is why the batch knob could not move the score, and it is why the arm's own smoke could falsify it in four minutes for free.
